name: nvm
description: Node Version Manager - POSIX-compliant bash script to manage multiple active node.js versions. $nvm: 3ArcxqLtXMmBnWbbtfwQgVL3MNnDsggzgGDtXMnjpump
one_liner: A free, essential command-line tool that lets developers install and switch between different versions of Node.js on the same computer. Note: the scraped GitHub description above ends with what looks like a pump.fun crypto token address unrelated to the actual project — that text appears to be spam/vandalism on the repo listing, not a real feature, and we're not treating it as one.
buyer: There's no real buyer here — nvm is free, foundational developer infrastructure that virtually every Node.js shop already uses; nobody pays for it and nobody could plausibly charge for it.
business_use_cases: A web dev agency uses it internally so every project can pin its own required Node version without conflicts — purely internal tooling, not a product.
A bootcamp includes it in every student's setup instructions as the standard way to manage Node versions.
A CI/CD pipeline uses it (or its logic) to test a library against multiple Node versions before release.

money_ideas.idea: None realistic — this is unmonetizable community infrastructure, and the crypto-token text appended to its description is very likely an attempt to abuse the project's visibility, not a legitimate business signal.

steal_this: Nothing to build from this repo — it's a dependency everyone already has, not a product opportunity. Ignore the crypto-token string in the description entirely; do not use it or link to it.
